bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Middle East crisis prolongation impacting SupTech government budgets/pipelines (monitoring post-June); Regulator caution on public AI adoption for confidential data; Execution risk in scaling MSME loan aggregation; Competitive intensity from AI-native entrants (currently low).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously Optimistic; Disciplined on capital allocation; Strategic focus on recurring revenue quality over sheer volume; Watchful on geopolitics but confident in product moat.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management is developing 'sovereign/private LLM' solutions to bypass regulator reluctance on public cloud AI for sensitive financial data; Days receivable improved to 75-80 days due to regulator payment discipline, a rare positive in government-facing businesses.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Long-standing domain position in regulatory technology: 'For a long time, IRIS has kept pace with this evolution, building the expertise, platforms and capabilities needed to help shape what comes next.'
- Flagship RegTech product IRIS Carbon 'continued to strengthen its position in international markets', giving an established international reference base
- Credibility proof point of running its own annual report on the IRIS CARBON Disclosure Management Platform - 'trust what we build and build what we trust'
- Standard-setting presence of the promoter-CEO: representation at the IFRS Taxonomy Consulting Group of the IASB, the XBRL sub-committee of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, and the SFIO steering committee on fraud prediction models
- Sticky regulator relationships in SupTech, described as 'a stable and strategically important segment', supported by sustained demand from regulators and public authorities
- Shift towards recurring revenue and enterprise SaaS, giving greater revenue visibility within a product-led model
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Integration with fragmented legacy infrastructure at customers and regulators — Many large financial institutions and supervisory authorities still run fragmented legacy systems, making deployment of modern compliance platforms operationally complex and resource intensive; the report states these integration challenges often impact implementation timelines, interoperability and enterprise-wide scalability - directly affecting revenue recognition timing and project cost for a platform vendor.
- Data quality and interoperability across multi-jurisdiction reporting — Inconsistent data quality, fragmented information systems and multi-jurisdictional reporting misalignment are flagged as persistent industry problems that can impact reporting accuracy, automation efficiency and regulatory responsiveness - the exact outcomes IRIS platforms are bought to deliver.
- AI governance and explainability exposure — As AI is embedded into compliance workflows, regulators and enterprises are emphasising auditable, explainable and traceable systems, particularly in high-risk workflows where automated decisions require clear accountability; this raises the product and assurance bar for an AI-led roadmap.
- Margin moderation from a sustained investment phase — The Board's Report states operating margins moderated versus the prior year mainly due to continued investments in product development, technology, infrastructure, sales and marketing, and talent acquisition to support long-term growth - so revenue growth is not currently translating into operating leverage.
- Earnings quality distorted by a one-time divestment gain — The Board explicitly cautions that the gain on disposal of the TaxTech / GST ASP business is non-recurring in nature and that the Company's underlying operating performance should be viewed separately from the one-time impact of the divestment.
- High export and international concentration — Exports contributed 81% of total turnover in FY26 and the client base spans 55 countries, with international delivery through subsidiaries in the USA, Singapore, Malaysia and Italy - concentrating the business in cross-border regulatory cycles, currency movements and foreign procurement decisions.
- Data security and privacy obligations on sensitive regulatory data — IRIS handles regulatory and disclosure data for regulators, banks and corporates in an environment the report describes as facing rising cyber threats, data breaches and tightening data-governance regimes such as the DPDP Act; the Company mitigates through ISO 27001:2022 and SOC 2 Type II certifications, but a security failure would be reputationally decisive for a compliance vendor.
- Early-stage ESG data and governance maturity — This is the Company's first BRSR, published voluntarily, with several practices described as remaining partial rather than fully operational, Scope 3 emissions based on spend-based estimates, and no external assurance obtained - leaving disclosure quality dependent on future build-out as ESG reporting obligations widen.

business.body: IRIS builds software platforms that convert regulatory compliance and corporate disclosure into structured, machine-readable and increasingly AI-assisted processes. The business is organised across SupTech (digital reporting, data collection, validation and supervisory technology for regulators and public authorities), RegTech (disclosure management, sustainability and structured financial reporting for enterprises, led by the IRIS Carbon platform) and DataTech. Following the strategic divestment of its TaxTech / GST ASP business, the Company is focused on a scalable, product-led model with increasing emphasis on recurring revenues, global markets and enterprise SaaS offerings.

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Sharpen the portfolio on RegTech, SupTech and DataTech by divesting the TaxTech business to the multinational firm Sovos UK, where management believes differentiation is strongest and long-term growth prospects most compelling.
- Transition to a platform-led model in which recurring revenues form the backbone of the business, providing greater visibility, resilience and scalability.
- Scale the IRIS CARBON Disclosure Management Platform as a global growth engine, building on referenceable customers across the United States and Europe and extending into new geographies such as Brazil.
- Evolve SupTech from a filing platform into a broader supervisory lifecycle ecosystem spanning data collection, validation, risk-based supervision, workflow management, and licensing and registration - the lifecycle platform regulators are seeking as they modernise supervisory infrastructure.
- Expand SupTech internationally across Asia, the Middle East and Africa, where the Company already has a strong reference base.
- Develop corporate tax returns as a further regulatory vertical for the SupTech solution, following the General Tax Authority (GTA), Qatar mandate.
- Broaden IRIS iDEAL in BFSI by bundling an ETL process to enable end-to-end regulatory reporting.
- Embed AI across the product stack - IRIS Instant (AI-driven XBRL generation, launched May 2025), an automated AI-driven iXBRL generation tool in progress, the newly launched RegAI platform that assimilates regulations across disciplines and analyses disclosures for compliance conformity, and 'Niti', an intelligence layer for reporting workflows.
- Achieve AI fluency in the software development and testing process to improve engineering productivity and shorten feature release cycles.
- Build the DataTech / IRIS Peridot MSME ecosystem - tools, visibility and financial access in a single mobile-first experience - supported by lending partnerships and government collaborations, extending the core competence of transforming data into decision-grade information.
- Invest in engineering, product and domain talent and multidisciplinary capability across regulation, data science and artificial intelligence.
- Voluntarily adopted the BRSR framework and published the Company's first Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report for FY 2025-26, ahead of the threshold at which it becomes mandatory, treating FY 2025-26 as a foundation year for formal ESG reporting.
- Adopted two new Board-approved policies - an Environmental Policy and a Human Rights Policy - and amended the Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption (ABAC) Policy to add a Policy Advocacy section, so the policy framework now aligns with all nine NGRBC principles.
- Mapped every policy against the nine NGRBC principles and assessed how far each has been translated from policy into documented procedure.
- Streamlined ESG governance under a BRSR Committee chaired by an Independent Director alongside two senior management members, with an annual review mechanism for ESG performance and commitments.
- Established named internal ownership for ESG data - Admin, Finance, HR, Company Secretarial, CSR and IT - with templates and processes for consistent year-on-year collection.
- Purchased electricity accounts for effectively all directly attributable Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions (196.01 tCO2e in FY 2025-26); the Company will work towards office-wise electricity intensity visibility, pursue energy efficiency across premises, and evaluate sourcing renewable electricity where lease terms and locations allow.
- FY 2026-27 priority: extend policy commitments to the value chain, including formal ESG screening of vendors and business partners.
- FY 2026-27 priority: improve Scope 3 coverage and methodology, moving from spend-based estimates to activity-based data for Business Travel and Employee Commuting, the two additional categories identified as material.
- FY 2026-27 priority: translate the newly adopted Environmental and Human Rights Policies, and other principles currently marked 'Partial', into documented operational procedures.
- FY 2026-27 priority: build sustainable and responsible sourcing practices into vendor and procurement processes.
- Commitment to conduct a formal enterprise-wide materiality assessment using the Company's own IRIS Carbon ESG platform so future disclosures are grounded in a structured assessment.
- Redundant IT equipment - laptops, servers and peripherals - is disposed of through CPCB-certified e-waste recycling vendors under the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022, and single-use plastics are being phased out of office pantries and event materials under the Environmental Policy.
- Holds ISO 27001:2022 and SOC 2 Type II certifications covering data security and privacy; no offices are located in water-stressed or ecologically sensitive areas.
- As an IT product company with no manufacturing, no owned vehicles and no combustion equipment, operations are inherently low-emission, with hybrid and remote working embedded in the Business Continuity Plan reducing commuting and office energy demand.
- Women represent 16.67% of the Board of Directors and 32% of permanent employees; permanent-employee turnover was 12.20% in FY 2025-26.
- The BRSR is prepared on a standalone basis covering IRIS RegTech Solutions Limited only, and no external assurance has been obtained on it.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: IRIS is an asset-light software products business, so its expansion is expressed as product build-out, market entry and talent rather than plant or capacity projects; the annual report contains no plant, line or capacity commissioning programme. The defining capital event of FY26 was the divestment of the TaxTech / GST ASP business, undertaken to simplify operations, sharpen focus on core growth areas and strengthen the Company's financial position; management states the proceeds and gains strengthened the balance sheet, improved liquidity and provided additional flexibility to invest in core growth areas such as SupTech, RegTech and enterprise SaaS. The Founders' message frames the same point as expansion capacity: 'The divestment strengthened our ability to invest in product innovation, market expansion and leadership talent while maintaining a strong balance sheet and pursuing growth without the need to look for additional resources.' Spending during the year went into product development, technology, infrastructure, sales and marketing, and talent acquisition, which is why operating margins moderated even as revenue grew. On the product roadmap, IRIS Instant - an automated AI-driven XBRL generation tool - was launched in May 2025, an automated AI-driven iXBRL generation tool is on track, and the newly launched RegAI platform can assimilate regulations across multiple disciplines and analyse disclosures for compliance conformity, with the ability to combine with IRIS CARBON. The Company also intends to achieve AI fluency in its own software development and testing process, where it has already seen productivity improvements and reduced feature release times.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Structural shift in which regulation is becoming a data ecosystem: across capital markets, central banks, business registries and tax authorities, periodic form-based reporting is giving way to structured, machine-readable and increasingly real-time data flows.
- Supervisory authorities are adopting technology-enabled approaches to reduce oversight lag, improve risk visibility and move towards continuous supervision, increasing demand for SupTech lifecycle platforms.
- Enterprises face increasing disclosure obligations across financial, regulatory and sustainability reporting and are seeking integrated platforms that manage the entire reporting lifecycle - drafting, collaboration, review, validation and filing - within a single environment.
- Recurring revenue mix continues to rise, improving revenue visibility and resilience; annual recurring revenue expanded by nearly 35% during the year.
- Margins moderated as the Company consciously increased investments across product engineering, sales and marketing - a deliberate decision to build capability, talent and market presence for the next phase of growth.
- Demand headwinds flagged by management: geopolitical uncertainties, cautious technology spending and longer decision cycles created a more demanding environment in some markets.
- AI is a demand catalyst: The Global State of RegTech 2026 notes 44% of financial institutions expect AI agents to be among the highest areas of compliance investment and 60% of RegTech vendors expect AI-led compliance solutions to attract the strongest technology spending in 2026.
- Cloud-native SaaS delivery is displacing on-premises compliance infrastructure through faster development cycles, lower implementation costs and API-driven integration.
- ESG RegTech is a growth vector as sustainability disclosure moves from voluntary to mandatory under frameworks such as CSRD, ISSB standards and climate-risk disclosure regulations.
- Indian RegTech market is projected to grow at a CAGR of 30.58% between FY25 and FY32, from nearly USD 628 million in FY24 to over USD 5.3 billion by FY32, supported by RBI, SEBI and IRDAI oversight expansion, DPDP Act compliance and the RBI FREE-AI framework.
- Global RegTech market was valued at approximately USD 19.06 billion in 2025 and is expected to reach USD 105.23 billion by 2034, a CAGR of 20% (Fortune Business Insights).
- Industry friction points that can slow conversion: integration with fragmented legacy infrastructure, inconsistent data quality and interoperability, and AI explainability / governance expectations.
- Mandate from Qatar Central Bank in SupTech.
- Mandate from the General Tax Authority (GTA), Qatar, towards corporate tax returns - described as a promising new regulatory vertical for the SupTech solution.
- Mandate from the International Financial Services Authority, Gift City, India.
- Significant enterprise mandate in Brazil for ESG and Disclosure Management, extending presence into a new high-potential geography.
- Referenceable IRIS CARBON customers across the United States and Europe, with the Disclosure Management Platform having moved beyond early adoption into established product-market fit.
- Strong existing reference base positioning the Company for SupTech opportunities across Asia, the Middle East and Africa.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: IRIS RegTech posted steady 23% FY26 revenue growth with a strengthened balance sheet (INR 155cr cash) post-TaxTech divestment, pivoting capital toward aggressive SaaS ARR expansion (targeting 35% CAGR) and AI-enabled product enhancements. The strategic shift prioritizes high-margin recurring revenue in global disclosure management while maintaining SupTech as a cash-flow stabilizer, though Middle East tensions pose a monitored risk to government project pipelines.
